small_guidance:
- Add autotune configs with smaller BLOCK_SP (32, 64) paired with larger num_warps (8, 16) — the current OC=64 forces a [64, BLOCK_SP] accumulator which at BLOCK_SP=512 means 32K-element tiles per program; smaller spatial tiles may improve occupancy on the 4090.
- Try fusing the bias add into the accumulator initialization (`acc = b_val[:, None].broadcast_to(...)`) to skip the post-loop add, and explore `tl.dot(..., allow_tf32=True)` explicitly. Also try a BLOCK_OC=32 variant with a reduction loop over two OC tiles, tracking running min — this halves register pressure.
- Add a key for `BLOCK_OC` and include cache-eviction hints (`eviction_policy='evict_last'` on weights, since the weight tile [OC, IC] is reused across all spatial programs of the same batch).
large_guidance:
- Switch from one-program-per-(N, spatial-tile) with BLOCK_OC=OC to a true im2col GEMM tiling: program grid (N, ceil(OH*OW / BLOCK_M)), reduce over GEMM-K (IC*KH*KW) inside the kernel with BLOCK_K=32 or 64. Since OC=64 fits in one BLOCK_N, the reduction (min across OC) can still be done in-register after the K-loop, but the K-loop with smaller tiles gives much better cache behavior than the current (KH*KW) outer × IC inner structure.
- Consider channels-last input layout (NHWC) so the IC dimension is contiguous; the current NCHW gather has stride_xc=H*W which hurts L1 reuse. Permute x once per forward (cheap relative to conv) and rewrite the address math.
- Persist the weight tile [OC, K] in shared memory once per program (it's only 64*144*4=36KB — fits) instead of reloading per (kh, kw); combine with a single K-loop sweep over all 144 reduction elements.
